note: Ps106 confession-recital (48v, 186 spans). Read by CHAR-ARC. Arcs: A praise+plea v1-5; B confession thesis 'we have SINNED' v6; C Red Sea (didn't CONSIDER/REMEMBER, REBELLED->BELIEVED/SANG) v7-12; D wilderness (FORGOT, wouldn't WAIT, WANTON CRAVING, TESTED, ASKED) v13-15; E ENVY of Moses v16; F golden calf (WORSHIPED, EXCHANGED glory, FORGOT) v19-21; G despised land (DESPISED, no FAITH, MURMURED, disobeyed) v24-25; H Baal-Peor+Phinehas (YOKED, PROVOKED->INTERVENED, RIGHTEOUSNESS) v28-31; I Meribah (ANGERED, bitter SPIRIT, SPOKE-RASHLY) v32-33; J Canaanite idolatry (didn't DESTROY, MIXED, LEARNED, SERVED idols, SACRIFICED sons, POURED innocent blood, POLLUTED, UNCLEAN, WHORE) v34-39; K judgment cycle (HATED, OPPRESSED, SUBJECTION, REBELLIOUS, PURPOSES, INIQUITY) v41-43; L mercy+plea (CRY, GIVE-THANKS, GLORY, BLESSED, PRAISE) v44-48. Between = God's acts (qualifiers) + imagery (standalone).

dims.v: v1: 'PRAISE (halal) the LORD! Oh give thanks to the LORD, for he is good' - the opening Hallelujah of the confession-hymn.
v1: 'Oh GIVE THANKS (yadah) to the LORD, for he is good' - gratitude for God's enduring love, the frame around the confession.
v2: 'or DECLARE (shama) all his praise?' - the rhetorical reach of proclaiming God's mighty deeds, more than any can utter.
paired with observing justice and doing righteousness
v3: 'BLESSED (esher) are they who observe justice' - the happiness of the just, set before the confession as the standard the fathers failed.
paired with the blessedness and righteousness
v3: 'they who OBSERVE (shamar) justice' - the keeping of justice, righteous conduct.
v3: 'they who observe JUSTICE (mishpat)' - the justice the blessed keep, righteous dealing.
v3: 'who do RIGHTEOUSNESS (tsedaqah) at all times!' - the constant right conduct of the blessed, the ideal against which Israel's history is confessed.
in the gladness of God's nation
v5: 'that I may REJOICE (samach) in the gladness of your nation' - the psalmist's longing to share his people's joy in God's favour.
v5: 'in the GLADNESS (simchah) of your nation' - the joy of the redeemed people the psalmist longs to share.
v5: 'that I may GLORY (halal) with your inheritance' - the psalmist's desire to exult with God's people, boasting in him.
v6: 'Both we and our fathers have SINNED (chata)' - the confession's thesis, the whole nation owning its guilt across the generations.
v6: 'we have COMMITTED INIQUITY (avah)' - the twisting of the right, the second term of the threefold confession.
v6: 'we have DONE WICKEDNESS (rasha)' - the active wrong, the confession's full admission of guilt.
paired with not remembering his love
v7: 'Our fathers... did not CONSIDER (sakal) your wondrous works' - the failure to weigh God's deeds, unbelief born of inattention.
paired with not considering, and with rebelling
v7: 'they did not REMEMBER (zakar) the abundance of your steadfast love' - the forgetting of God's love that bred rebellion.
paired with the failure to remember
v7: 'but REBELLED (marah) by the sea, at the Red Sea' - the first act of the catalogue, defiance at the very edge of deliverance.
v12: 'Then they BELIEVED (aman) his words' - the flash of faith after the sea's deliverance, belief that would not last.
v12: 'they SANG (shir) his praise' - the song of the redeemed at the sea, worship soon forgotten (v13).
paired with not waiting for his counsel
v13: 'But they soon FORGOT (shakach) his works' - the swift forgetting, the song of v12 dying within days.
v13: 'they did not WAIT (chakah) for his counsel' - the impatience that would not trust God's timing.
paired with the craving and the testing
v14: 'But they had a WANTON (taavah) craving in the wilderness' - the fierce appetite that ruled them, desire become idolatry.
v14: 'they had a wanton CRAVING (avah) in the wilderness' - the lusting after food, the greed that tested God.
v14: 'and put God to the TEST (nasah) in the desert' - the presumptuous trying of God born of appetite.
paired with the craving God granted
v15: 'He gave them what they ASKED (sheelah)' - the demand God met, granting their request but sending leanness.
paired with the earth swallowing the rebels
v16: 'When men in the camp were JEALOUS (qana) of Moses' - the envy of Korah's company against God's chosen leaders.
v19: 'and WORSHIPED (shachah) a metal image' - the calf-worship at Horeb, the exchange of the living God for an idol.
the glory of God for an ox-image
v20: 'They EXCHANGED (mur) the glory of God for the image of an ox' - the fatal swap, the Creator traded for a grass-eating beast.
v21: 'They FORGOT (shakach) God, their Saviour, who had done great things in Egypt' - the forgetting of the very God who redeemed them.
v24: 'Then they DESPISED (maas) the pleasant land' - the scorn of Canaan at Kadesh, rejecting God's gift.
v24: 'having no FAITH (aman) in his promise' - the unbelief that could not trust God to give the land.
v25: 'They MURMURED (ragan) in their tents' - the grumbling of the people, discontent turned to complaint against God.
v25: 'and did not OBEY (shama) the voice of the LORD' - the disobedience behind the murmuring.
v28: 'they yoked themselves to the Baal of PEOR (peor)' - see char yoked; the Baal-place. Standalone.
paired with the plague and Phinehas' intervention
v29: 'they PROVOKED (kaas) the LORD to anger with their deeds' - the rousing of God's wrath, met by plague.
paired with the righteousness counted him
v30: 'Then Phinehas stood up and INTERVENED (palal), and the plague was stayed' - the zeal of Phinehas, decisive action that turned back the wrath.
v31: 'And that was counted to him as RIGHTEOUSNESS (tsedaqah)' - the reckoning of Phinehas' zeal to his everlasting credit.
v32: 'They ANGERED (qatsaph) him at the waters of Meribah' - the provoking at Meribah, whose fallout reached even Moses.
paired with the bitterness and rash speech
v33: 'for they made his SPIRIT (ruach) bitter' - Moses' inner self soured by the people's strife, the meekest man goaded.
paired with the spirit and rash words
v33: 'they made his spirit BITTER (marah)' - the embittering of Moses, provocation working inward.
v33: 'and he SPOKE RASHLY (bata) with his lips' - Moses' hasty words at Meribah, the one lapse that cost him the land.
v34: 'They did not destroy the PEOPLES (am)' - the Canaanite nations spared (char destroy, 307469 handled). Standalone.
v35: 'but they MIXED (arab) with the nations' - the intermingling with the peoples, compromise that bred corruption.
to do as the nations did
v35: 'and LEARNED (lamad) to do as they did' - the adoption of pagan ways, sin caught by association.
paired with the idols that snared them
v36: 'They SERVED (abad) their idols, which became a snare to them' - the idolatry that trapped the people.
their sons and daughters to demons
paired with pouring out innocent blood
v37: 'They SACRIFICED (zabach) their sons and their daughters to the demons' - the child-sacrifice, idolatry at its most horrific.
v38: 'they POURED OUT (shaphak) innocent blood, the blood of their sons and daughters' - the shedding of innocent blood, murder as worship.
v38: 'and the land was POLLUTED (chaneph) with blood' - the defilement of the land by their bloodshed.
v39: 'Thus they became UNCLEAN (tame) by their acts' - the defilement of the people themselves, sin as pollution.
v39: 'and played the WHORE (zanah) in their deeds' - the spiritual adultery of idolatry, unfaithfulness to God imaged as harlotry.
v41: 'those who HATED (sane) them ruled over them' - the enmity of the nations to whom God gave his people over.
paired with bringing them into subjection
v42: 'Their enemies OPPRESSED (lachats) them' - the affliction of Israel under the nations, the fruit of their sin.
v42: 'and they were brought into SUBJECTION (kana) under their power' - the humbling of Israel, abased beneath their foes.
v43: 'but they were REBELLIOUS (marah) in their purposes' - the persistent defiance, deliverance met again with rebellion.
v43: 'rebellious in their PURPOSES (etsah)' - the self-devised counsels the people preferred to God's will.
v43: 'and were brought low through their INIQUITY (avon)' - the guilt that sank them, sin bearing its own judgment.
paired with God hearing and remembering
v44: 'when he heard their CRY (rinnah)' - the cry of the afflicted that moved God to remember his covenant.
paired with glorying in his praise
v47: 'that we may GIVE THANKS (yadah) to your holy name' - the vow of the gathered people, the aim of the plea to be saved.
v47: 'and GLORY (shabach) in your praise' - the exulting in God the gathered would render.
the LORD, the God of Israel
v48: 'BLESSED (barak) be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting!' - the doxology closing Book IV.
v48: 'Let all the people say, Amen! PRAISE (halal) the LORD!' - the closing Hallelujah, the whole people's Amen.

v7: 'the abundance of your STEADFAST LOVE (chesed)' - God's covenant love. Qualifier.

v8: 'for his NAME'S (shem) sake' - God's name. Qualifier.
